preconditions.description: n is the number of photos to select (3 to 1000), and m is the number of albums (1 to 40).

preconditions.expression: len(album_counts) == m and all(1 <= a <= 1000 for a in album_counts)
preconditions.description: The input provides exactly m integers representing the count of photos in each album, each between 1 and 1000.

postconditions.expression: is_impossible or (len(result) == n and all(1 <= x <= m for x in result) and all(result[i] != result[(i + 1) % n] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, output a sequence of n album IDs (1 to m) such that no two adjacent photos (including the wrap-around from last to first) belong to the same album. If no such sequence exists, output -1.
A solution is impossible if and only if the count of photos in the most frequent album exceeds the maximum number of non-adjacent slots available in a cycle of size n, which is ceil(n/2).

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and all(result.count(i + 1) <= album_counts[i] for i in range(m))
postconditions.description: If a solution is found, the number of times each album ID appears in the result must not exceed the available count of photos in that album.
